rows: Q4 intentional marketing over-investment vs budget
Celsius share of energy-category dollar growth (2022)
A couple percentage points (on club piece)
Record Q4 sales of $178M (+71%) and FY2022 revenue of $654M (+108%); FY North America +126%.
Celsius was the #1 brand driver of energy-category growth (22% of category dollar growth, ~$474M incremental retail sales) and the #3 US energy drink.
Dominant theme: the completed PepsiCo distribution transition; ACV jumped from the mid-60s to the high-80s (~89.7%); no further material distributor-transition charges anticipated.
$194M of FY2022 distributor termination expense ($156M Q3, $38M Q4), funded by Pepsi, plus a deliberate ~$15M Q4 marketing over-investment (~$48M incremental for the full year).
Gross margin improved to 44.4% in Q4 (+~445 bps YoY), achieving management's mid-40s exit-rate goal.
Three strategic pillars outlined: top-line growth, operational excellence, and cash generation / EBITDA leverage.

Gross margin gains driven by lower average can prices, improved freight lanes from the orbit model and Pepsi transition, and pricing benefits; Q4 pricing carries across 2023, no new 2023 price increase announced.

Central friction: reconciling reported 74% Q4 North America growth versus ~130% Nielsen scan growth - attributed to the Q3 pipe-fill, year-end customer destocking and incomplete transition; pipe-fill add-back would lift growth above 90%.
FY2022 operating cash flow of $108M (vs -$97M in 2021); cash of $653M bolstered by the PepsiCo partnership injection.
The $282.5M non-deductible Series A preferred-stock valuation adjustment (amortized as contra revenue over 20 years) distorted the effective tax rate.
Continued unresolved 2021 material weaknesses; an unfavorable January 2023 Flo Rida litigation verdict under appeal; a can-label settlement expected to close by end of Q2.
Club channel sales $138M (+247%); inline-packing transition (started Q4, expanding Q1) plus pack-size upsizing (15-pack to 18-pack) are 2023 margin levers.
New national rollouts in Q1 2023: Aldi (~600+ stores) and BJ's; second SKUs at Costco and Sam's Club.
Large non-tracked distribution upside: the Pepsi OTS/'medals' independent program (~150,000 doors) and foodservice (~1,600 colleges, ~1,600 hospitals).
Func Food (FAST) brand name was impaired; FAST snack portfolio focused on Finland with no current Pepsi distribution discussions.
Management signaled intent to announce additional international expansion initiatives in additional countries in the future, though North America remains the priority.
Erythritol exposure is a very minor part of the portfolio (estimated under ~1% of sales); management 'looking into it' following recent stroke/heart-attack news.
Cooler payback period ~5 months; sales increase 'exponentially' with cold placement within 60 feet of the register.
Reconciling North America Growth vs. Scan Data
Reconcile the gap between reported North America sales growth (+74%) and Nielsen scan growth (~+130%); where does the company ultimately land on ACV / total distribution / non-tracked channels?

CFO said the pipe-fill would have brought North America growth above 90%; year-end working-capital management by big customers likely pulled inventories down, and scan data remains accurate (Q1 continues to accelerate). CEO said ACV finished ~89-90% with great transition execution; additional ACV expected from spring resets, Bang space capture, club (BJ's) and foodservice - declined to give forward ACV guidance.
Distribution Points, Shelf Placement & Pipe-Fill Math

Actual distribution points (not ACV) for 2023, what is secured for spring resets, whether product goes into existing energy coolers or dedicated functional coolers; reconcile the pipe-fill puts and takes.

Reported distribution ~210,000 doors, with considerable incremental opportunity in non-reported channels (foodservice, the Pepsi OTS/medals program with ~150,000 doors), Tier 3/4 accounts and new markets; product goes into core energy shelf space. Adding the $15-20M pull-forward back to Q4 approximates a normalized run rate, though year-end inventory control and incomplete transition during the quarter are offsets.
Selling Expense Run Rate & International Timing
How much of the increased selling expense was incremental and what is the right go-forward run rate; why is now the right time to start talking about international?

The company strategically went ~$15M over budget in Q4; historically S&M runs ~23-23.5%, and backing out the $15M over-spend and $38M transition fees returns Q4 to ~22% of revenue. CFO confirmed Q1 2023 back to ~22%. On international, opportunities exist via Pepsi and existing Nordics/APAC partners, but North America remains the priority.
Is the 'quarterly acceleration' comment broad-based or is QTD growth actually stronger than the ~90%+ Q4 growth; how does the 44%+ exit rate inform 2023 gross margin?

The acceleration comment referred to Nielsen scan and IRI SPINS data, not forward guidance on Q1. The mid-40s exit-rate goal was achieved for the entire quarter; with expensive cans behind them and freight-lane and raw-material benefits, a mid-40s gross margin throughout 2023 remains valid, with upside opportunity preferred but the range maintained given commodity uncertainty.
Drivers behind the Amazon channel detail/softness and how the channel has trended in early 2023.

Amazon grew strongly for the year ($58M, +83%); in the quarter there were warehouse-movement-related inventory shifts around the holiday season that potentially caused delays, but no major inventory challenges. Amazon expected to remain a strong omnichannel business alongside Instacart and home delivery.

Where were Q4 ACV gains filled geographically and what is left; how to think about the lag between entering a new geography and optimal consumption; productivity of stores with vs without an owned cooler.

Pre-PepsiCo Celsius was ~65-67% ACV, concentrated regionally; the Pepsi transition opened ACV broadly (center of the country, Pacific Northwest, Mid-Atlantic), supported by the Q4 marketing over-investment, reaching ~89-90% nationwide. Cooler payback period ~5 months; sales increase 'exponentially' with cold placement 60 feet from the register.
Where will SKU count grow most by channel and half; latest thoughts on Pepsi and club distribution efficiency; will more price be taken in 2023?

Average items per store ~12.5 and expected to keep rising with resets, but declined to commit to a landing point - better visibility after April data. Club inline-packing transition (started Q4, expanding Q1) will help margin; Q4 pricing benefits carry across 2023; no 2023 price increase announced.
Club Channel Margin Upside & Reset Placement
Order of magnitude of margin-improvement upside from the club efficiency initiatives - hundreds of basis points possible? Will resets also yield better physical shelf placement?

Full benefit requires consolidating all club volume into the same co-packers (not yet complete, expected this year); upside 'could be a couple percentage points' on the club piece, a small part of the business - plus freight-lane gains (annualized freight down from ~6% to ~4% over two years). CEO said the goal is to move out of the 'gutter'/'nosebleed' into the 'bullseye' placement, targeting vacated Bang space.
Func Food / FAST Brand, PepsiCo Snack SKUs & Aldi
What is going on with the Func Food impairment and the FAST brand; do PepsiCo food/protein SKUs create SKU-expansion discussion; country-specific flavors for international; Aldi rollout scope?

Celsius Europe (Sweden/Finland) had a great Q4 with new innovation; the FAST snack portfolio is focused on Finland with no current PepsiCo distribution discussions - some European protein-bar raw-material supply-chain challenges. Aims for more strategic, consistent flavor launches across regions. Aldi national rollout underway across roughly 600+ stores and growing.

Confirm the 20,000 dedicated Celsius cooler target by end of 2023, how many placed in Q4 2022; how many of the ~50,000 Pepsi energy coolers Celsius is in and the year-end goal; how much of the portfolio contains erythritol?

Confirmed the 20,000+ dedicated Celsius cooler target with ~15,000 currently on order. Roughly 4,500-5,000 dedicated coolers in place by end of 2022 (placements held back during the transition). On Pepsi energy coolers, no current count given but the goal is the majority (ideally all ~50,000) by year-end. Erythritol is a very minor part of the portfolio (likely under ~1% of sales); 'we're looking into it.'
How much of the PepsiCo transition is actually converted versus available - is the company '100% available but only 60% converted'?

'Transition complete' refers to distribution partners - ~90-95% of North America is now serviced by PepsiCo, with a few prior distributors retained, essentially 100% complete on the October 1, 2022 agreement. ACV reached ~89% of reported stores with considerable additional upside (deferring a finish-year estimate to April data), plus large non-reported upside in the ~150,000-door OTS/medals program and foodservice.
